modules.title: Basics of Deep Learning and Foundation Models
Cutting-edge AI Applications
modules.tagline: Connect AI to the real world

lessons.title: AI Overview
lessons.intro: Artificial intelligence studies methods and systems that simulate and extend human intelligence. Machine learning is one way to implement AI; deep learning is a branch of machine learning. The course also introduces different schools of thought, so AI should not be reduced to neural networks alone.
lessons.example: A rules-based expert system represents Symbolism. A neural image classifier reflects Connectionism. A robot that adapts through perception and action illustrates Behaviorism.
lessons.trap: An AI application is not automatically a deep-learning application. Strong AI is a theoretical category in this course, not a claim about every capable chatbot.
lessons.memory: AI is the field; ML learns; DL uses deep neural networks.
lessons.arabic: AI هو المجال الكبير. ML طريقة بنتعلم بيها من البيانات، وDL جزء من ML بيعتمد على Neural Networks عميقة. مش كل AI لازم يكون Neural Network.

concepts.explanation: Deep learning belongs within machine learning, which belongs within AI. This is a relationship of inclusion rather than three interchangeable names.
concepts.question: Which relationship correctly places deep learning within the broader field?
concepts.answer: DL is a subset of ML, and ML is a subset of AI
distractors: AI is a subset of DL
Every AI system is a deep neural network

concepts.explanation: Symbolism uses explicit symbols, mathematical logic and inference. Expert systems connect stored knowledge with rules.
concepts.question: A system reasons over explicit facts and rules. Which school best matches this design?

concepts.explanation: Connectionism starts from neurons and their connections. Neural networks implement learning through connected processing units.
concepts.question: A researcher models intelligence using connected artificial neurons. Which school is this?

concepts.explanation: Behaviorism emphasizes perception, action and interaction with the environment. Intelligence is expressed through adaptive behavior.
concepts.question: Which school places perception-action interaction at the center of intelligence?

concepts.explanation: Data supplies experience, algorithms define learning procedures and computing power makes the computations possible. None of these alone defines the whole AI system.
concepts.question: Which resource is the engine that executes AI computations?

lessons.title: AI Technologies
lessons.intro: AI technologies solve different kinds of input-output problems. NLP processes human language, CV processes visual information and multimodal systems relate more than one modality. Foundation models are trained at scale and can be adapted to multiple downstream tasks.
lessons.example: For a street image, classification names the scene, detection locates cars, segmentation labels pixels and tracking associates a car across video frames. OCR reads the registration text.
lessons.trap: Detection is not segmentation. A foundation model is not defined merely by running on a GPU. A token count measures training data, not the number of model parameters.
lessons.memory: NLP: language. Detection: boxes. Segmentation: pixels. Tracking: across time.
lessons.arabic: NLP بيتعامل مع اللغة وCV مع الصور. Detection بيحدد مكان الجسم، وSegmentation بيقسم الصورة على مستوى Pixels، وTracking بيتابع الجسم بين Frames.

concepts.explanation: Text classification assigns a category to a text; sequence labeling assigns labels to sequence elements; text generation produces new text.
concepts.question: Assigning a sentiment category to a customer review is which task?

concepts.explanation: Detection finds and locates objects; segmentation assigns region or pixel labels; tracking maintains object identity across frames; OCR extracts text.
concepts.question: A system must identify the same vehicle in successive video frames. Which task is central?

concepts.explanation: A knowledge graph represents entities and relationships in a structured network, allowing a system to use connections rather than isolated facts.
concepts.question: What is explicitly represented by the links between entities in a knowledge graph?

concepts.explanation: Large-scale data, model capacity and compute support broad representation and generalization. Pretraining builds a reusable base; fine-tuning adapts it. Scaling law, emergence and the Chinchilla discussion connect model size, data and behavior.
concepts.question: A broadly pretrained model is adapted using domain-specific data. What is the adaptation stage called?

concepts.explanation: Multimodal processing combines or relates text, images, audio or video. Cross-modal understanding maps information between modalities, such as describing an image in text.
concepts.question: Which task directly combines visual and language information?
concepts.answer: Producing a textual description of an image

lessons.title: Overview of DeepSeek and Its Influence on AI Development
lessons.intro: This section is a historical snapshot of DeepSeek in the training material, not a live product ranking. It traces the launch, coding and chat models, V2, V3 and reasoning development, then explains the industry effects of efficient algorithms and open sharing.
lessons.example: The timeline places the DeepSeek launch in July 2023, V2 in May 2024 and V3 in December 2024. Read reported cost and popularity numbers as dated course claims, with their stated scope.
lessons.trap: Do not treat reported training expense as a complete lifetime development cost, or historical benchmark statements as a current ranking.
lessons.memory: DeepSeek: timeline + efficiency + openness + industry impact.
lessons.arabic: هنا بنذاكر DeepSeek زي ما اتعرض في الكورس وقت إعداده. الفكرة الأساسية كفاءة التدريب وOpen-source وتأثيرهم على المنافسة، مش ترتيب النماذج النهارده.

concepts.explanation: The material associates the launch of DeepSeek by Liang Wenfeng with July 2023. Later releases build on this timeline.
concepts.question: In which year does the course place the launch of DeepSeek?

concepts.explanation: The timeline places DeepSeek-V2 in May 2024. Keep V2 distinct from the later V3 release.
concepts.question: Which release does the course place in May 2024?

concepts.explanation: The course places V3 in December 2024 and describes a 671-billion-parameter model, with MoE among the efficiency-related techniques.
concepts.question: Which architecture is specifically associated with DeepSeek efficiency in the material?

concepts.explanation: The material names Multi-Head Latent Attention, auxiliary loss-free load balancing and Multi-Token Prediction alongside MoE. Distinguish these course terms from unrelated preprocessing operations.
concepts.question: Which technique is named in the DeepSeek technology discussion?

concepts.explanation: Open sharing can lower adoption barriers, enable reuse and feedback, and intensify competition. The course stresses algorithm, application and talent development rather than compute alone.
concepts.question: Which outcome best reflects the course discussion of open-source AI?

lessons.title: AI Applications
lessons.intro: AI applications have expanded from perception and understanding to content generation and multi-task assistance. The appropriate task depends on the business problem and available data. The course uses mining, nature conservation, government, weather, drug development and coding as concrete examples.
lessons.example: Audio collected in a natural habitat can support wildlife monitoring. Weather observations can support forecasting. A code assistant instead processes programming-related context to generate or explain code.
lessons.trap: A useful application is not proof of human-level general intelligence. Match the technology to the data and task rather than assuming every use case is image classification.
lessons.memory: Identify the input, the task and the useful output.
lessons.arabic: في أي Application اسأل: البيانات إيه؟ المشكلة إيه؟ والمطلوب يطلع إيه؟ تسجيلات أصوات في محمية غير صور أشعة وغير توقعات طقس.

concepts.explanation: Generative AI creates outputs such as text, images or code. Perception applications primarily recognize or interpret existing inputs.
concepts.question: An assistant drafts a new report from a request. Which capability is central?

concepts.explanation: The application discussion contrasts specialized tasks with systems that can support several related tasks through broad language capabilities.
concepts.question: Which example best illustrates multi-task assistance?
concepts.answer: One assistant summarizes, translates and drafts text
distractors: A calculator with one fixed formula only

concepts.explanation: The course presents sound-based environmental and wildlife monitoring. Audio can provide evidence about species and environmental events.
concepts.question: Which input most directly fits the course example of a shield of sound for wildlife protection?

concepts.explanation: Meteorology is an AI4Science application in which data and models support weather prediction. Its output is not a language label by definition.
concepts.question: Predicting future atmospheric conditions is an example of AI applied to which field?

concepts.explanation: Coding assistance applies AI to code-related tasks, while requiring evaluation appropriate to the software task. Generated output is not automatically verified.
concepts.question: Which output best fits an AI coding assistant?
concepts.answer: A proposed function implementing a requested behavior
distractors: A guarantee that every program is correct

lessons.title: Debates and Future of AI
lessons.intro: AI adoption creates questions about trust, privacy, data security, employment and ethical responsibility. Generated content can be plausible without being authentic. The course also discusses future value, AGI, embodied intelligence and increasingly personalized and multimodal applications.
lessons.example: A realistic generated recording may imitate a person without documenting a real event. A useful service therefore needs verification and responsible handling of the data used to build it.
lessons.trap: A convincing output is not evidence of truth. Open-source availability does not remove obligations involving privacy, security or content rights.
lessons.memory: Useful AI still needs trustworthy data and responsible use.
lessons.arabic: كون الصورة أو الصوت مقنع مش معناه إنه حقيقي. لازم نفصل جودة التوليد عن صحة المعلومة، ونفكر في Privacy وSecurity وحقوق المحتوى.

concepts.explanation: Generative systems can create convincing synthetic media. Appearance alone cannot establish that an event really happened.
concepts.question: Why does realistic AI-generated video create an authenticity challenge?
concepts.answer: Visual plausibility does not establish a real event
distractors: Every realistic video is a camera recording
Video cannot be edited by AI
All generated video is clearly watermarked

concepts.explanation: Personal data requires careful collection, use and protection. Training and application deployment both create potential data-handling concerns.
concepts.question: Uploading private records without appropriate safeguards most directly raises which concern?

concepts.explanation: Fairness, explainability and transparency matter alongside usefulness. A strong task score does not alone establish responsible behavior.
concepts.question: Which evaluation goes beyond predictive accuracy?

concepts.explanation: Artificial general intelligence concerns broad capabilities across tasks. The course presents it as a future technology direction rather than an automatic property of any chatbot.
concepts.question: Which term refers to a broad general intelligence ambition?

concepts.explanation: Embodied AI links intelligent processing to interaction with a physical environment, including sensing and acting.
concepts.question: Which system most directly illustrates embodied AI?
concepts.answer: A robot that perceives objects and manipulates them

lessons.title: Machine Learning Algorithms
lessons.intro: Machine learning improves task performance through experience. In the E-T-P definition, experience is what the system learns from, the task is what it must do and performance is how success is measured. Learned models approximate an unknown relationship rather than receiving every rule explicitly.
lessons.example: For spam detection, E is previously labeled mail, T is classifying new mail and P can be classification accuracy. For house-price prediction, the target is a numerical price rather than a category.
lessons.trap: Experience is not the accuracy score. Classification uses discrete targets even when class names are represented by numbers.
lessons.memory: E = experience; T = task; P = performance.
lessons.arabic: E البيانات أو الخبرة اللي بنتعلم منها. T المهمة المطلوبة. P المقياس اللي بيقول أداءنا اتحسن ولا لأ.

concepts.explanation: Experience is the data or interaction history used for learning. It is distinct from the objective task and its evaluation metric.
concepts.question: A spam filter learns from labeled historical emails. What represents E?
distractors: The act of predicting a label

concepts.explanation: The task describes what the learning system must do with a sample. Classifying emails and predicting prices are different tasks.
concepts.question: A handwriting model is evaluated by recognition accuracy. What is its task T?

concepts.explanation: Performance measures task success, for example accuracy or error. A task can be evaluated using different metrics.
concepts.question: Which item is a performance measure P for a classifier?

concepts.explanation: Traditional rule-based systems use explicitly programmed rules. ML is useful when rules are complex, difficult to specify or change with the data.
concepts.question: Which situation most strongly motivates machine learning?
concepts.answer: Decision rules are difficult to specify but examples exist
distractors: One exact arithmetic rule already solves the task
No data or feedback can ever be obtained

concepts.explanation: Classification predicts discrete categories; regression predicts continuous quantities; clustering groups unlabeled examples using similarity.
concepts.question: Predicting a numerical apartment price is which task?

lessons.title: Types of Machine Learning
lessons.intro: Learning types differ in the experience and feedback available. Supervised learning uses known targets. Unsupervised learning searches for patterns without target labels. Semi-supervised learning combines labeled and unlabeled data. Reinforcement learning improves actions through interaction and reward.
lessons.example: A medical image classifier with expert labels is supervised. Grouping unlabeled customers is unsupervised. A robot selecting actions based on outcomes and rewards is reinforcement learning.
lessons.trap: Unsupervised learning is not defined as learning from rewards. A small labeled subset plus many unlabeled examples is semi-supervised, not fully supervised.
lessons.memory: Labels supervise; similarity groups; reward guides actions.
lessons.arabic: Supervised عنده Labels. Unsupervised بيدور على أنماط من غير Labels. Semi-supervised خليط. Reinforcement فيه Agent بياخد Actions وبيتعلم من Reward.

concepts.explanation: The training examples include targets. The model learns a mapping from features to a label or numerical output.
concepts.question: Training on images paired with known species labels is which learning type?

concepts.explanation: Examples have no supplied target labels. Clustering uses internal similarity to discover groups.
concepts.question: Grouping unlabeled shoppers by purchase patterns is which learning type?

concepts.explanation: A limited labeled set is combined with a larger unlabeled set. This addresses the cost of annotation while using available data.
concepts.question: A dataset has 300 labeled images and 20000 unlabeled images used together for learning. Which approach fits?

concepts.explanation: An agent acts in an environment, observes states and receives rewards. Learning aims to improve the action strategy over time.
concepts.question: A robot learns whether to recharge or keep cleaning based on consequences and rewards. Which approach fits?
distractors: Supervised regression with fixed labels only

concepts.explanation: Both are commonly supervised prediction tasks. The distinction concerns the target: category versus continuous value, not whether the input contains numbers.
concepts.question: Predicting whether a transaction is fraudulent is which supervised task?

lessons.title: Machine Learning Process
lessons.intro: The ML lifecycle starts with suitable data and ends with deployment and iteration. Cleaning resolves missing, invalid, noisy or inconsistent records. Feature engineering converts inputs into useful representations. Training, validation and testing serve different roles and must not be treated as interchangeable.
lessons.example: A classifier has TP=40, FP=10 and FN=20. Precision is 40/(40+10)=0.80; recall is 40/(40+20), approximately 0.667. These metrics answer different questions.
lessons.trap: The test set is not the place to repeatedly select hyperparameters. Filter methods do not train a new model for each candidate subset; wrapper methods do.
lessons.memory: Train learns; validation selects; test estimates generalization.
lessons.arabic: Training بيتعلم Parameters. Validation بنختار بيه الإعدادات. Test بنقيس بيه التعميم في الآخر. Precision بيسأل تنبؤاتي الإيجابية صح قد إيه، وRecall لقيت كام من الإيجابيات الحقيقية.

concepts.explanation: Missing data, noise, inconsistent formats and invalid duplicates can damage learned patterns. Preprocessing may include cleaning, conversion, standardization and dimensionality reduction.
concepts.question: Which issue is directly addressed by data cleansing?
distractors: Choosing the number of Transformer heads

concepts.explanation: Filter methods score features independently of the model; wrappers evaluate subsets with a predictive model; embedded methods select features during fitting, such as LASSO.
concepts.question: Which approach trains predictive models to score candidate feature subsets?

concepts.explanation: Training estimates parameters, validation supports selection and tuning, and the test set measures generalization after those choices.
concepts.question: Which dataset should guide hyperparameter selection?

concepts.explanation: Excess capacity relative to useful data can lead to low training error and poor generalization. High bias commonly signals insufficient fitting; high variance signals sensitivity to training samples.
concepts.question: A model is excellent on training examples but poor on new examples. What is the likely problem?
distractors: Insufficient model capacity in every case

concepts.explanation: Precision equals TP/(TP+FP); recall equals TP/(TP+FN). Accuracy uses all correct predictions. MAE and MSE evaluate numerical prediction error.
concepts.question: With TP=40 and FP=10, what is precision?

lessons.title: Important Machine Learning Concepts
lessons.intro: Gradient descent updates parameters in the negative gradient direction. Learning rate controls the update size. Batch methods differ in how many samples contribute to an update. Hyperparameters control learning and model configuration, while parameters are learned from data.
lessons.example: With weight w=2, gradient=3 and learning rate=0.1, one gradient-descent step gives 2-0.1×3=1.7. In 5-fold cross-validation, each fold serves as validation once.
lessons.trap: A fold count is a hyperparameter. Gradient descent is an optimization method, not the only possible way to estimate every model.
lessons.memory: Update = old value minus learning rate times gradient.
lessons.arabic: Gradient Descent بينزل عكس اتجاه Gradient. Learning Rate بيحدد حجم الخطوة. Parameters بيتعلمها الموديل، Hyperparameters بنحددها أو بنختارها بالبحث وValidation.

concepts.explanation: The gradient points toward increasing local objective value; a descent step subtracts a learning-rate-scaled gradient.
concepts.question: If w=2, gradient=3 and learning rate=0.1, what is the updated weight?

concepts.explanation: BGD uses all training samples per update, SGD uses one and mini-batch uses a smaller group. They trade update stability against computational cost.
concepts.question: Which method uses a small subset of samples for each parameter update?

concepts.explanation: Learned weights are parameters. Learning rate, batch size and search configuration are hyperparameters; their values may be selected by a search procedure.
concepts.question: Which item is normally learned during network training?

concepts.explanation: Grid search enumerates configured combinations. Random search samples configurations and can be more suitable in large search spaces.
concepts.question: A method evaluates every combination in a specified hyperparameter grid. What is it?

concepts.explanation: k-fold validation rotates the held-out fold and trains on the remaining folds. The held-out test set remains separate for final evaluation.
concepts.question: In 5-fold cross-validation, how many times does each fold serve as validation?

lessons.title: Common Machine Learning Algorithms
lessons.intro: Algorithm choice depends on the target, data structure, interpretability and resource needs. The course explains linear and logistic models, decision trees, margin-based SVMs, neighbor-based methods, probabilistic classification, ensembles and clustering. Several algorithms can support more than one task; avoid learning a rigid one-algorithm-one-task table.
lessons.example: Random Forest combines decision trees using bagging. GBDT builds learners sequentially to correct earlier errors. In k-NN, k is a neighbor count; in k-means, k is a cluster count.
lessons.trap: Logistic regression is a classifier despite its name. Bagging and boosting are not interchangeable. Polynomial regression can be nonlinear in features while remaining linear in its coefficients.
lessons.memory: Logistic classifies; SVM separates; k-NN votes; k-means groups.
lessons.arabic: Logistic Regression للتصنيف رغم اسمه. Random Forest أشجار متعددة بطريقة Bagging، وGBDT بيتعلم بالتتابع. k في k-NN عدد الجيران، وفي k-means عدد Clusters.

concepts.explanation: Linear regression predicts numerical targets. Logistic regression uses sigmoid for binary classification; softmax generalizes to multiple classes. L1 is associated with LASSO and L2 with Ridge.
concepts.question: Which model is directly suited to a binary class probability?
distractors: Ordinary linear regression without a classifier

concepts.explanation: Trees split examples using feature tests and purity measures such as entropy or Gini. SVM chooses a separating boundary with a large margin; kernels support nonlinear separation.
concepts.question: Which method explicitly seeks a maximum-margin separating boundary?

concepts.explanation: k-NN uses nearby stored examples; a very small k can be noise-sensitive. Naive Bayes uses a conditional-independence assumption for features given the class.
concepts.question: What is the key simplifying assumption in Naive Bayes?
concepts.answer: Features are conditionally independent given the class
distractors: Every feature is a neural-network weight

concepts.explanation: Bagging trains base learners independently and combines results. Random Forest uses bagging with trees; boosting is sequential, with GBDT correcting errors through later learners.
concepts.question: Which method builds later learners to correct the errors of the current ensemble?

concepts.explanation: k-means iterates assignments and centers to reduce within-cluster variation. Hierarchical clustering forms nested groups through aggregation or splitting.
concepts.question: Which value must be supplied to basic k-means as the desired number of groups?

lessons.title: Perceptron
lessons.intro: A perceptron receives inputs, weights their contributions, adds a bias or compares with a threshold, and produces an output. Its simple decision boundary is linear. Combining layers with nonlinear functions enables patterns that one linear boundary cannot represent.
lessons.example: AND can be separated by one line in a two-input plot. XOR places its two positive cases on opposite corners, so one straight boundary cannot separate them from both negative cases.
lessons.trap: Stacking only linear transformations still gives an overall linear transformation. Extra layers need nonlinear activations to add nonlinear representational power.
lessons.memory: One linear boundary cannot separate XOR.
lessons.arabic: Perceptron بيجمع Inputs بعد ضربها في Weights ومعاها Bias. XOR محتاج فصل غير خطي، فمجرد طبقات Linear فوق بعض مش كفاية.

concepts.explanation: Each input is multiplied by a weight. The bias shifts the activation threshold or boundary without needing an extra varying input feature.
concepts.question: What is the value before activation for x=3, w=2 and b=-1?

concepts.explanation: A single perceptron performs linear separation in its input space. Its success depends on the separability of the task.
concepts.question: Which task cannot be solved by a single linear perceptron in the original two-input space?

concepts.explanation: Bias provides an offset in the weighted-sum computation. It is a learned model parameter in standard neural models.
concepts.question: Which quantity shifts the decision boundary independently of the input values?

concepts.explanation: AND, NAND and OR operations can be combined through intermediate units to implement XOR. Intermediate layers transform the representation.
concepts.question: Why can a multi-layer nonlinear network solve XOR?
concepts.answer: Intermediate nonlinear representations permit non-linear separation
distractors: Every added layer removes all weights

concepts.explanation: A composition of affine layers without nonlinearities remains affine. Nonlinear activations make the overall mapping more expressive.
concepts.question: What is missing if adding many linear layers still cannot model a nonlinear relationship?

lessons.title: Fully-connected Neural Network and How It Is Trained
lessons.intro: A fully-connected feedforward network transforms input through hidden layers to an output. Training alternates prediction, loss calculation, gradient calculation and parameter updates. Backpropagation uses the chain rule; an optimizer uses the resulting gradients. Activation functions, optimizer choice and regularization influence whether the model can learn and generalize.
lessons.example: For a multiclass network, logits can be converted into a probability distribution by softmax. If training error falls while validation error rises, early stopping can prevent continuing into a worse-generalizing model.
lessons.trap: Backpropagation computes gradients; it is not the optimizer update. Dropout is a training regularizer and should not remain randomly active in ordinary evaluation.
lessons.memory: Forward predicts; loss measures; backward differentiates; optimizer updates.
lessons.arabic: Forward بيطلع التوقع وLoss بيقيس الخطأ. Backpropagation بيحسب Gradients، وبعدها Optimizer بيحدّث Weights. Validation بيكشف Overfitting.

concepts.explanation: Sigmoid maps to (0,1), tanh to (-1,1), ReLU returns max(0,x), Leaky ReLU retains a small negative slope and Swish uses a sigmoid gate.
concepts.question: Which activation returns zero for negative inputs and the input itself for positive inputs?

concepts.explanation: The chain rule propagates derivatives from the loss through earlier computations. It provides parameter gradients for optimization.
concepts.question: Which training stage computes gradients through the network using the chain rule?

concepts.explanation: Softmax converts a vector of logits into positive class probabilities summing to one, commonly for multiclass outputs.
concepts.question: What property should a softmax output vector have?
distractors: Its length always equals the batch size

concepts.explanation: Momentum stabilizes and accelerates updates in consistent directions. AdaGrad adapts rates using accumulated squared gradients; RMSProp uses decay; Adam tracks first and second moments.
concepts.question: Which optimizer maintains first- and second-moment estimates of gradients?

concepts.explanation: L1 encourages sparsity, L2 penalizes large weights, dropout randomly suppresses activations during training and early stopping monitors validation behavior.
concepts.question: Training loss falls while validation loss persistently rises. Which action directly addresses this pattern?
distractors: Tune repeatedly on the final test set

lessons.title: Convolutional Neural Network
lessons.intro: A CNN extracts local patterns with convolutional filters. Shared weights reuse a filter at many spatial locations, reducing parameters relative to dense connections. Pooling reduces spatial dimensions. Features can be flattened and passed to fully-connected layers for classification.
lessons.example: For a 5×5 input, a 3×3 kernel, stride 1 and no padding, each output spatial dimension is (5-3)/1+1=3. A 2×2 max-pooling window over [1,4;2,3] outputs 4.
lessons.trap: Output channels count learned filters, not the number of classes in every layer. Pooling downsamples; it is not the same operation as learned convolution.
lessons.memory: Convolution extracts; pooling shrinks; dense layers decide.
lessons.arabic: CNN بيستخدم Filters على أجزاء صغيرة من الصورة، ونفس Weights بتتكرر مكانيًا. Pooling بيقلل الأبعاد، وFully-connected بيستخدم Features في التصنيف.

concepts.explanation: A convolutional neuron connects to a local region rather than every input pixel. Local features can build into more global patterns through layers.
concepts.question: Which CNN idea limits a neuron to a local patch of the input?

concepts.explanation: The same filter weights are applied at different spatial positions. This reuses the same pattern detector and limits the parameter count.
concepts.question: Why can a CNN detect the same local pattern at multiple image positions with one filter?
concepts.answer: The filter weights are shared across positions
distractors: Every pixel has a separate classifier
The test labels move with the image
Pooling learns a new label per pixel

concepts.explanation: For dilation one, output size is floor((input+2×padding-kernel)/stride)+1. Padding and stride change spatial dimensions.
concepts.question: What is the output width for input width 5, kernel 3, stride 1 and padding 0?

concepts.explanation: Max pooling selects the largest value in a window; average pooling computes its mean. Both summarize nearby activations.
concepts.question: What does 2×2 max pooling produce from values 1,4,2,3?

concepts.explanation: A typical pipeline applies convolution and activation, pooling, flattening and fully-connected classification. A feature map is the activation response of a filter.
concepts.question: Which operation converts spatial features into a vector for a dense layer?

lessons.title: Model Architecture Based on the Recurrent Neural Network
lessons.intro: RNNs model ordered data by combining the current input with a hidden state from the previous step. This recurrence shares computation across time but restricts parallel processing. LSTM introduces a cell state and gates to better control information flow. Seq2Seq uses an encoder and decoder to transform one sequence into another.
lessons.example: In translation, an encoder reads source words and the decoder produces target words. In basic fixed-context Seq2Seq, compressing a long sentence into one fixed-size vector can lose information.
lessons.trap: Cell state and hidden state are different LSTM quantities. RNN steps depend on earlier states. Decoder output length need not equal encoder input length.
lessons.memory: RNN remembers a state; LSTM gates a cell; Seq2Seq maps sequences.
lessons.arabic: RNN بيستخدم Hidden State من الخطوة اللي فاتت. LSTM بيضيف Cell State وGates للتحكم في المعلومات. Seq2Seq فيه Encoder وDecoder ومش لازم طول الناتج يساوي المدخل.

concepts.explanation: At time t, hidden state depends on the current input and previous hidden state. This makes sequence order relevant.
concepts.question: What is used with the current input to compute a basic RNN hidden state?
distractors: A future hidden state already known

concepts.explanation: The forget gate uses a sigmoid-controlled selection to retain or discard parts of the previous cell state. Values near zero suppress information.
concepts.question: Which LSTM gate controls retention of the old cell state?

concepts.explanation: The input gate controls new information written to the cell. The output gate controls what is exposed from the processed cell state as the hidden output.
concepts.question: Which LSTM gate controls the new candidate information added to cell memory?

concepts.explanation: The encoder represents the source sequence; the decoder uses that representation to generate the target sequence. BOS and EOS mark sequence boundaries.
concepts.question: In a translation encoder-decoder, which component generates the target sequence?

concepts.explanation: Fixed-size context can discard information from long inputs. RNN recurrence also limits parallelization because each step needs a previous state.
concepts.question: What is a key limitation of basic fixed-context Seq2Seq on long sentences?
concepts.answer: Compressing the input into one fixed-size vector can lose information
distractors: Input and output must always be the same word
Every token can be processed independently of prior state

lessons.title: Transformer Architecture
lessons.intro: Attention builds a representation by weighting relevant values. It compares a query with keys, normalizes scores and takes a weighted sum of values. Self-attention applies this process within the same sequence. The original Transformer uses attention-based encoder and decoder stacks instead of recurrent computation.
lessons.example: When interpreting a pronoun, self-attention can assign stronger weight to the noun it refers to. Positional information matters because attention alone does not inherently encode word order.
lessons.trap: The original Transformer is encoder-decoder; later model families can use one stack. Parallel training does not mean autoregressive generation emits every output token simultaneously.
lessons.memory: Query asks; keys match; values contribute.
lessons.arabic: Attention بيقارن Query مع Keys، يحول Scores لأوزان بـSoftmax، ويجمع Values بالأوزان دي. Self-attention المقارنة فيه داخل نفس Sequence.

concepts.explanation: Query describes what is sought, keys support relevance matching and values provide the information combined in the result.
concepts.question: Which attention components are compared to obtain relevance scores?

concepts.explanation: Scores are normalized using softmax and used as weights in a sum of values. The output depends on content relevance.
concepts.question: After converting attention scores into weights, what operation produces the attention result?

concepts.explanation: Self-attention computes relationships among elements of the same sequence. Cross-attention connects different source and target representations.
concepts.question: Comparing each word with other words in the same input sentence is which mechanism?

concepts.explanation: The original 2017 architecture contains encoder and decoder stacks with attention, feed-forward blocks and residual normalization structure. Position information is supplied separately.
concepts.question: Which component provides token-order information in the Transformer architecture shown in the course?

concepts.explanation: Attention connects positions directly and supports more parallel training computation than sequential recurrence. Autoregressive decoding still conditions on previous outputs.
concepts.question: Why does an RNN have a training parallelism constraint that attention helps reduce?
concepts.answer: Each recurrent state depends on the preceding state
distractors: Every Transformer has fewer parameters than every RNN

lessons.title: Basic Foundation Model Architecture
lessons.intro: Transformer-based foundation models reuse a broad pretrained representation for downstream tasks. GPT-1 uses a decoder-style stack, while BERT uses bidirectional encoder representations. Mixture-of-Experts expands capacity using multiple expert components and a gating mechanism rather than treating every input identically.
lessons.example: A gate can route an input to selected experts. Total model capacity and the amount of computation used by one input are therefore different concepts.
lessons.trap: BERT and GPT are not identical stacks. MoE routing is not random bagging. A reported BERT parameter count can refer to a particular configuration, not every BERT variant.
lessons.memory: BERT encodes; GPT generates; MoE routes.
lessons.arabic: GPT في الشرح Decoder-style، وBERT بيعتمد على Encoder وBidirectional Context. MoE فيه Experts وGate بيختار المناسب للمدخل.

concepts.explanation: A foundation model learns broad patterns from large-scale data and can be adapted. Reuse avoids independently training every task model from the beginning.
concepts.question: What is a key purpose of reusing a pretrained foundation model?
concepts.answer: Adapt broad learned representations to downstream tasks
distractors: Eliminate the need for any data

concepts.explanation: The course describes GPT-1 as using the Transformer decoder framework, retaining masked attention and feed-forward structure.
concepts.question: Which Transformer branch underlies GPT-1 in the course?

concepts.explanation: BERT uses bidirectional context and encoder-style Transformer representations. The material associates its release with 2018.
concepts.question: Which description best matches BERT in the course?

concepts.explanation: When shared parameters serve different data subsets or tasks, updates for one can affect another. Capacity and routing influence this interference.
concepts.question: What does interference describe in shared multi-task learning?
concepts.answer: Updates for one task can affect another task
distractors: All tasks always have identical data
Each task owns completely unrelated hardware

concepts.explanation: MoE combines expert components with a gating mechanism that selects or balances their contributions, increasing effective capacity and efficiency.
concepts.question: What controls expert selection in MoE?

lessons.title: AI Framework
lessons.intro: An AI framework supplies reusable APIs for data handling, model construction, differentiation, training, evaluation and deployment. It also translates a model into executable computations and schedules them on hardware. The material introduces PyTorch, TensorFlow and JAX, while showing the wider framework landscape.
lessons.example: A developer defines a network using high-level layers. The framework manages many underlying tensor computations and gradient operations, rather than requiring a hand-written derivative implementation for each layer.
lessons.trap: PyTorch is software; CPU and GPU are hardware. CUDA is a computing platform, not a physical device. Framework capabilities vary by version.
lessons.memory: Framework = APIs + computation + training + deployment support.
lessons.arabic: Framework بيجهزلك Tensor Operations وLayers وAutograd وTraining Tools. PyTorch برنامج، إنما CPU وGPU Hardware، وCUDA مش قطعة Hardware.

concepts.explanation: Frameworks support data processing, model construction, debugging, training, evaluation, conversion and deployment. These functions span a lifecycle.
concepts.question: Which responsibility belongs to an AI development framework?
concepts.answer: Supporting model training and automatic differentiation

concepts.explanation: Encapsulated APIs provide reusable layers and operations, letting developers describe algorithms without implementing every low-level detail.
concepts.question: Why do developers use framework layer APIs?
distractors: To guarantee all training data is correct

concepts.explanation: PyTorch offers tensor computation, Python-oriented development, dynamic graphs and automatic differentiation. It supports training on CPUs and GPUs.
concepts.question: Which pair names physical devices usable for PyTorch training?

concepts.explanation: TensorFlow is an end-to-end ML platform. TensorFlow.js supports JavaScript environments; the material presents TensorFlow Lite for on-device inference.
concepts.question: Which tool is associated with JavaScript-based TensorFlow development?

concepts.explanation: JAX combines NumPy-like numerical APIs, automatic differentiation and XLA-based compilation for efficient computation on supported accelerators.
concepts.question: Which combination best describes JAX in the material?
concepts.answer: NumPy-like APIs, automatic differentiation and XLA
distractors: Only image annotation and manual rules

lessons.title: Basics of AI Development Frameworks
lessons.intro: Tensors are multidimensional data arrays; operators transform them. A computational graph connects operations through directed data dependencies. Frameworks use graphs to represent and execute models and compute derivatives. Dynamic and static graph modes differ in when the computation structure is built.
lessons.example: An image batch in NCHW order can have shape [8,3,32,32]: eight RGB images, each 32 by 32. In a computational graph, matrix multiplication is an operator and its inputs and outputs are tensors.
lessons.trap: Tensor rank is the number of axes, not the length of one axis. PTH is not ONNX. A static graph is not a model with permanently frozen weights.
lessons.memory: Tensors carry data; operators transform it; graphs connect operations.
lessons.arabic: Tensor مصفوفة متعددة الأبعاد. Shape أحجام المحاور وRank عددها. Operator عملية، وComputational Graph بيوضح العمليات والاعتماد بينها.

concepts.explanation: Scalars have rank 0, vectors rank 1 and matrices rank 2. Shape lists axis sizes; dtype describes the stored element type.
concepts.question: What is the rank of a tensor with shape [8,3,32,32]?

concepts.explanation: Image batches often use [N,C,H,W]; sequence tensors can use [batch,sequence,feature]. Layout must agree with the layer interface.
concepts.question: In NCHW image layout, what does C represent?
distractors: Number of classes in every case

concepts.explanation: Nodes represent operations and directed edges carry tensor dependencies. The representation supports execution, optimization and automatic differentiation.
concepts.question: In a computational graph, what does an addition node represent?

concepts.explanation: A dynamic graph is constructed while operations execute. A static graph is defined before execution and can expose a fixed structure for optimization.
concepts.question: Which graph style is constructed during program execution?
distractors: Static graph defined entirely in advance

concepts.explanation: PyTorch commonly uses .pt or .pth for saved models or state. ONNX is an exchange representation; file extensions alone do not establish the exact saved content.
concepts.question: Which format is intended for model interchange across supported tools?

lessons.title: PyTorch
lessons.intro: PyTorch separates data loading, model definition, loss and optimization. Dataset provides examples and DataLoader supplies batches. A subclass of nn.Module defines layers in __init__ and computation in forward. Autograd computes gradients; the optimizer updates trainable parameters. The course builds LeNet using MNIST and then saves and reloads the result.
lessons.example: One batch follows: clear gradients → compute predictions → compute loss → backward → optimizer step. After loading a state_dict into the same architecture, use evaluation mode and disable gradient recording for ordinary inference.
lessons.trap: model.eval() changes module behavior but does not itself disable gradient recording. optimizer.step() does not replace loss.backward(). A state_dict does not define the Python model architecture.
lessons.memory: Zero → forward → loss → backward → step.
lessons.arabic: Dataset بيجيب Sample وDataLoader بيجمع Batches. backward بيحسب Gradients وstep بيحدّث Parameters. eval بيغير سلوك Layers، وno_grad بيوقف تسجيل Gradients.

concepts.explanation: Dataset defines sample access and transformations. DataLoader iterates batches and can shuffle sample order.
concepts.question: Which component supplies shuffled mini-batches during training?

concepts.explanation: nn.Module is the base class for networks. __init__ constructs layers and forward defines how data flows through those layers.
concepts.question: Which method defines a custom module forward computation?

concepts.explanation: loss.backward() calculates gradients. optimizer.step() uses available gradients to update parameters. zero_grad clears accumulated gradients for the usual batch loop.
concepts.question: Which statement updates model parameters using their computed gradients?

concepts.explanation: eval switches modules such as dropout into evaluation behavior. no_grad disables gradient recording; both have different roles.
concepts.question: Which operation disables gradient recording in a typical inference block?

concepts.explanation: state_dict stores parameter and persistent-buffer tensors. Loading it normally requires constructing a compatible network first.
concepts.question: What is needed before loading saved LeNet weights with load_state_dict?
distractors: Only the filename without an architecture

lessons.title: AI Application Development Process
lessons.intro: Application development connects a business objective to an executable model. The course follows requirement analysis, environment setup, data preparation, network construction, training and deployment. The ResNet-50 example adapts an image model to classify five flower types, with ModelArts as an optional cloud environment.
lessons.example: A pretrained image classifier can replace its final output layer with five outputs for the flower categories, then train or fine-tune using the task dataset. A small device may need compression before deployment.
lessons.trap: Training and inference have different resource and gradient needs. Pruning removes less important weights or units; distillation trains a smaller student using a teacher.
lessons.memory: Requirements → environment → data → network → train → deploy.
lessons.arabic: ابدأ بالمشكلة، جهز Environment وData، ابني Network ودربها وقيّمها قبل Deployment. Pruning بيشيل أجزاء أقل أهمية، وDistillation بينقل معرفة Teacher لـStudent أصغر.

concepts.explanation: Requirements define the task before model and environment choices. Data preparation and training precede evaluating and deploying the application.
concepts.question: Which step should clarify the problem before selecting a model?
distractors: Model compression before any task is defined

concepts.explanation: The course flower example uses a five-category dataset and discusses adapting a pretrained classifier output to the task.
concepts.question: A flower task has five mutually exclusive classes. How many class outputs should its classifier provide?

concepts.explanation: ModelArts provides development, training and deployment support when a local environment is unsuitable or unavailable.
concepts.question: Which Huawei service is presented as an optional cloud AI development environment?

concepts.explanation: Model pruning removes less important connections or units and trades model size against possible quality loss. It is not identical to teacher-student training.
concepts.question: Which compression method removes less important model connections?

concepts.explanation: A smaller student learns useful behavior from a larger teacher, aiming for similar task quality at lower computational cost.
concepts.question: A compact student learns from a large teacher model. Which method is this?

lessons.title: AI Business Process
lessons.intro: The business process begins by asking what problem must be solved and what value the result should provide. Data collection and preprocessing make the task learnable. Model selection, training and evaluation connect the requirement to a deployable system. Deployment is a lifecycle stage, not a substitute for assessing task quality.
lessons.example: For product recommendation, user behavior and product information are relevant data. For detecting objects in security images, visual data and task-specific labels are relevant. The business goal determines what to collect and evaluate.
lessons.trap: Do not choose a fashionable architecture before defining the task. A development framework and a trained business model are different things.
lessons.memory: Problem first; appropriate data next; evaluate before deployment.
lessons.arabic: Business Process يبدأ: إحنا بنحل إيه؟ بعدين نجمع ونجهز Data، نختار Model وندربه ونقيّمه وننشره.

concepts.explanation: Requirements identify the purpose and problem to solve, guiding data collection and model choice.
concepts.question: What should be clarified first in the AI business process?
concepts.answer: The problem and desired business outcome

concepts.explanation: Collected data must reflect the task, such as behavior data for recommendations or images for vision problems.
concepts.question: Which data is most directly relevant to personalized product recommendations?

concepts.explanation: Cleaning, organization, transformations and labeling prepare raw data for the selected task and model.
concepts.question: Which action belongs to data preprocessing?
concepts.answer: Resolving missing values and inconsistent records

concepts.explanation: Evaluation measures task quality and generalization using suitable metrics before operational use. Different tasks need different measures.
concepts.question: Why evaluate a trained model before deployment?
concepts.answer: To assess whether its behavior meets task requirements
distractors: To guarantee no future error is possible

concepts.explanation: Deployment integrates inference into the target environment so inputs can produce usable predictions. Inference does not ordinarily update weights.
concepts.question: What distinguishes ordinary model inference from training?
concepts.answer: It produces predictions without updating weights
distractors: It always performs backward and optimizer steps
It needs target labels for every prediction

lessons.title: Large Model Business Process
lessons.intro: Large models use a familiar lifecycle but magnify data, compute and evaluation demands. Broad pretraining is followed by task adaptation and alignment when required. The course covers data/tensor/pipeline parallelism, SFT, parameter-efficient tuning, reward models and RLHF. Evaluation spans capability, ethics/security and vertical-domain performance.
lessons.example: Data parallelism copies a model across devices and splits examples. Tensor parallelism splits tensors. Pipeline parallelism places different layers on successive devices. In RLHF, human rankings train a reward model that guides further language-model optimization.
lessons.trap: Prompt tuning trains added embeddings; writing a prompt does not. A reward model scores responses rather than simply acting as the original chatbot. Low-rank adaptation is not full-parameter retraining.
lessons.memory: Pretrain knowledge; fine-tune tasks; align preferences; evaluate broadly.
lessons.arabic: Pretraining يبني أساس، وFine-tuning يخصصه. LoRA بيدرّب Low-rank Matrices. RLHF بيستفيد من تفضيلات البشر وReward Model. Data Parallel يقسم البيانات، Tensor يقسم Tensors، وPipeline يقسم Layers.

concepts.explanation: Data parallelism replicates a model across devices with different examples; tensor parallelism partitions tensors; pipeline parallelism partitions layers across devices.
concepts.question: Each device holds the same model but trains on different mini-batches before gradients are combined. Which strategy is this?

concepts.explanation: Adapter tuning adds trainable modules. Prefix tuning adds trainable task prefixes; prompt tuning learns input embeddings. LoRA learns low-rank update matrices while the base is frozen.
concepts.question: Which method trains low-rank update matrices alongside frozen pretrained weights?

concepts.explanation: The illustrated process moves from supervised instruction fine-tuning to reward-model training from ranked responses, then reinforcement learning guided by that reward model.
concepts.question: What directly supplies supervision for the reward model in the course RLHF pipeline?

concepts.explanation: Alignment aims for helpful, honest and harmless behavior. Preference information shapes output behavior but does not guarantee perfect factuality.
concepts.question: Which group matches the 3H evaluation principles?

concepts.explanation: GLUE/SuperGLUE assess language understanding; GSM8K focuses on math word problems; MMLU spans disciplines. BLEU and ROUGE compare generated text with references. Domain and safety evaluation remain important.
concepts.question: Which benchmark is associated with mathematical word-problem solving?

lessons.title: Use of Large Models and Prompt Engineering
lessons.intro: Prompt engineering organizes instructions, context, examples and output requirements so a model can perform a task. Zero-shot gives no examples; few-shot supplies demonstrations. Chain-of-thought prompting adds intermediate solution steps, either through demonstrations or an instruction to work step by step.
lessons.example: Zero-shot: classify this review as positive or negative. Few-shot: show several review-label examples first. Few-shot-CoT: show worked examples with intermediate steps. Zero-shot-CoT: request stepwise solving without worked examples.
lessons.trap: Few-shot examples need not include reasoning. A request for steps without demonstrations is not few-shot. Writing a natural-language prompt does not itself train model weights.
lessons.memory: Shots count demonstrations; CoT adds intermediate steps.
lessons.arabic: Zero-shot من غير أمثلة. Few-shot فيه أمثلة. لو الأمثلة فيها خطوات حل يبقى Few-shot-CoT. لو طلبت Step by step من غير أمثلة يبقى Zero-shot-CoT.

concepts.explanation: State the task and constraints explicitly. Delimiters separate content from instructions, and a requested schema makes output easier to use.
concepts.question: Which change most directly improves an ambiguous extraction prompt?
concepts.answer: Specify the fields and required output structure
distractors: Assume the model knows every missing requirement

concepts.explanation: Zero-shot prompting supplies a task instruction without task demonstrations. The model relies on its learned capabilities and provided context.
concepts.question: A prompt gives a classification instruction and a new review, but no labeled examples. Which technique is this?

concepts.explanation: Few-shot prompting includes a small number of input-output demonstrations to establish the intended task pattern.
concepts.question: A prompt shows three review-label pairs before the new review. Which technique is this?

concepts.explanation: Worked demonstrations contain intermediate solution steps as well as answers, showing how to approach a reasoning task.
concepts.question: A prompt provides two worked arithmetic examples before a new problem. Which technique best fits?

concepts.explanation: A prompt requests stepwise solving without worked demonstrations. It changes the instruction rather than adding example solutions.
concepts.question: A prompt says to solve step by step but contains no demonstrations. Which technique is this?

lessons.title: Voice Assistants
lessons.intro: The course uses Celia to show how an assistant supports routines, entertainment and travel. Voice interaction connects a user request to language understanding and useful actions. Visual capabilities and links to other applications can extend the interaction beyond speech alone.
lessons.example: A traveler asks an assistant for help with a journey. The system must interpret the request and provide or coordinate a useful service, not merely transcribe a sound waveform.
lessons.trap: Speech recognition, understanding an intention and carrying out an action are different stages. A voice interface does not imply that all intelligence runs entirely on the device.
lessons.memory: Hear the request; understand the intent; assist with the task.
lessons.arabic: Voice Assistant لازم يفهم الطلب ويساعد في تنفيذه، مش بس يحول الصوت لنص. الكورس بيستخدم Celia في الروتين اليومي والترفيه والسفر.

concepts.explanation: Celia is the Huawei assistant featured in the material, with examples for daily routines, fun and travel.
concepts.question: Which assistant is the central voice-assistant example in the course?

concepts.explanation: Assistants can reduce friction in common tasks by interpreting natural-language requests and coordinating useful functions.
concepts.question: Which task most directly fits a daily-routine assistant?
concepts.answer: Helping act on a spoken reminder request

concepts.explanation: Understanding what the user intends is different from merely obtaining recognized words from audio.
concepts.question: After speech has been converted to text, what is needed to determine the requested task?

concepts.explanation: The broader assistant discussion includes voice and visual capabilities. Different input types support different interaction needs.
concepts.question: An assistant interprets a spoken request about an image. What capability is illustrated?

concepts.explanation: The course presents travel as a voice-assistant scenario. The task determines which information and connected services are useful.
concepts.question: Which scenario matches the travel-assistant discussion?
concepts.answer: Helping a user with a journey-related request
distractors: Eliminating all need for user instructions

lessons.title: Smart Homes
lessons.intro: Smart-home AI connects devices, user needs and environmental information. The material groups examples around making life easier, increasing comfort and helping users feel secure at home or away. The value comes from coordinated behavior rather than a list of disconnected devices.
lessons.example: Lighting and other home devices can respond to a user request or a relevant condition. Monitoring can provide information when the resident is away, while requiring appropriate handling of household data.
lessons.trap: Automation does not automatically mean advanced learning. Data protection remains relevant when sensors, cameras and connected services handle private household information.
lessons.memory: Ease + comfort + security through connected devices.
lessons.arabic: Smart Home بيربط Devices عشان يسهل الاستخدام ويحسن الراحة والأمان. وجود Sensors مش معناه إن Privacy مبقتش مهمة.

concepts.explanation: Smart-home applications coordinate devices and interactions around household needs.
concepts.question: What is central to a smart-home application?
concepts.answer: Coordinating connected devices for household tasks
distractors: Training every user as a programmer

concepts.explanation: Comfort-related automation adapts household behavior to useful conditions and preferences.
concepts.question: Which use case most directly concerns home comfort?

concepts.explanation: Convenient interaction reduces the number of manual actions needed for ordinary household tasks.
concepts.question: Which outcome best represents smart-home convenience?
concepts.answer: Controlling several home devices through one interaction
distractors: Requiring separate manual rewiring each time

concepts.explanation: Monitoring helps users understand relevant events at home, including while away.
concepts.question: Which scenario matches the course theme of reassurance at home and away?
concepts.answer: Receiving relevant home-monitoring information while absent

concepts.explanation: Connected sensors may capture sensitive household information. System usefulness and appropriate data handling both matter.
concepts.question: Which information requires particular privacy care in a smart-home system?

lessons.title: Intelligent Vehicles
lessons.intro: The material separates Qiankun Intelligent Driving from the HarmonyOS Cockpit experience. Driving intelligence supports driving-related perception and decisions, while the cockpit focuses on connected interaction, applications, audio and in-vehicle services. Celia contributes voice and visual interaction capabilities.
lessons.example: A voice request to an in-car entertainment service is a cockpit interaction. Sensing the road to support driving belongs to a different functional responsibility, even if both are in one vehicle.
lessons.trap: Do not equate an entertainment application with autonomous driving. Connected cockpit features do not prove that a vehicle can handle every road condition without supervision.
lessons.memory: Driving handles the road; cockpit handles the in-car experience.
lessons.arabic: Qiankun متعلق بالقيادة الذكية. HarmonyOS Cockpit متعلق بتجربة الكابينة والتطبيقات والتفاعل. الاتنين في العربية بس مش نفس الوظيفة.

concepts.explanation: Qiankun Intelligent Driving is the course example for intelligent driving capability.
concepts.question: Which name is associated with intelligent driving in the material?

concepts.explanation: The automotive operating system connects people, devices, audio and applications for an intelligent cockpit experience.
concepts.question: Which platform is presented for the intelligent cockpit?

concepts.explanation: Voice and visual interaction support a smarter in-vehicle experience. User intent must connect to an appropriate cockpit function.
concepts.question: Which assistant contributes voice and visual capabilities to the cockpit discussion?
distractors: BERT as a named vehicle product

concepts.explanation: Driving functions and in-vehicle entertainment have different tasks and outputs. One should not be used as evidence for the other.
concepts.question: Playing requested music through an in-car app is primarily which kind of function?
distractors: A guarantee of fully autonomous driving

concepts.explanation: The cockpit links people, applications and devices. Its purpose includes a richer travel and entertainment experience.
concepts.question: Which outcome matches the HarmonyOS Cockpit discussion?
concepts.answer: A connected in-vehicle application and audio experience
distractors: Elimination of all physical driving risks
A model that never needs evaluation
A replacement for every vehicle component

lessons.title: Intelligent Recommendation
lessons.intro: An intelligent recommender connects a user with useful items using behavior and contextual information. Knowledge graphs add structured entity relationships and background information. These links can diversify suggestions and make the reason for a recommendation easier to explain.
lessons.example: A user likes a film. The graph can connect it to other films through an actor, director or genre, producing more than a simple repetition of the same item type.
lessons.trap: Knowledge-graph edges represent semantic relationships, not necessarily neural-network weights. A recommendation should not rely on assuming that every new user already has a long interaction history.
lessons.memory: Entities + relationships provide paths to relevant items.
lessons.arabic: Knowledge Graph بيربط User وItems بActors أوGenres أوعلاقات تانية. ده يساعد في تنوع التوصيات وشرح سبب الترشيح وتقليل مشاكل Cold Start.

concepts.explanation: Entities are connected by explicit relationships that provide semantic background for recommendation.
concepts.question: What does a movie-to-director edge encode?

concepts.explanation: Behavior, interests and requirements can help build user profiles and match users to relevant items.
concepts.question: Which data most directly helps infer a user interest in a recommendation task?

concepts.explanation: Actor, director and genre links provide different routes from liked items to new items.
concepts.question: A new movie is recommended because it shares a director with a liked movie. What supports this explanation?
concepts.answer: A relationship path in a knowledge graph

concepts.explanation: A new user or item may have little interaction history. Auxiliary information can help reduce this recommendation difficulty.
concepts.question: What is the recommendation problem caused by little history for a new item?

concepts.explanation: Semantic links can broaden results and connect a recommendation to known user interests, improving interpretation and acceptance.
concepts.question: Which advantage does the material associate with knowledge-graph recommendation?
distractors: A guarantee every suggestion is accepted

lessons.title: Intelligent Robots
lessons.intro: Humanoid robots are potential carriers of embodied AI, connecting perception, cognition and action. Vision-Language-Action models incorporate visual-language capabilities into robotic control. The course discusses RT-2 and a diffusion foundation model for bimanual manipulation, RDT-1B.
lessons.example: A robot receives a command to pick the smallest object. It must combine visual identification, language interpretation and an action, potentially generalizing to objects not seen during its specific robot training.
lessons.trap: Generating a text description of an action is not by itself successful physical execution. Generalization must be evaluated on new objects and instructions.
lessons.memory: VLA = see + understand language + act.
lessons.arabic: VLA بيربط Vision وLanguage وAction. الروبوت لازم يشوف ويفهم التعليمات ويتصرف، ويقدر يتعامل مع Objects أوأوامر جديدة.

concepts.explanation: Robots couple intelligent computation with physical sensing and action in an environment. Humanoid form is one possible carrier.
concepts.question: Which property makes a robot a carrier of embodied AI?
concepts.answer: Physical interaction guided by perception and cognition
distractors: Saving text with a robot emoji

concepts.explanation: Vision-Language-Action models connect visual observations and language instructions with robot actions.
concepts.question: What does the A in VLA refer to?

concepts.explanation: The material uses RT-2 to show transfer from Internet-scale visual-language knowledge into robotic control.
concepts.question: Which system is cited as a Vision-Language-Action model in the robot section?

concepts.explanation: A robot can be tested on unfamiliar objects or instructions, such as choosing the smallest object. This tests more than repeating memorized trajectories.
concepts.question: A robot follows a new instruction involving an unseen object. Which capability is being tested?

concepts.explanation: The material references RDT-1B as a diffusion foundation model for bimanual manipulation. Bimanual concerns using two arms or hands.
concepts.question: Which task is associated with RDT-1B in the course?

lessons.title: AI4Science
lessons.intro: AI4Science applies learned models to scientific problems such as quantum systems, material discovery and molecular simulation. The course links neural-network research and protein modeling to the 2024 Nobel Prizes. These examples differ in scientific target and model role, so learn the mapping rather than one generic definition.
lessons.example: GNoME supports crystal discovery and stability prediction. MatterGen generates inorganic materials with desired properties. FermiNet and LapNet address quantum computations, while DeePMD-kit supports molecular dynamics.
lessons.trap: Material generation is not the same task as protein structure prediction. A scientific model output still needs domain-appropriate evaluation; it does not replace scientific validation.
lessons.memory: Fermi/Lap: quantum. GNoME/MatterGen: materials. DeePMD: dynamics.
lessons.arabic: AI4Science يعني نستخدم AI في مسائل علمية. FermiNet وLapNet للكوانتم، GNoME وMatterGen للمواد، DeePMD للحركة الجزيئية، وAlphaFold2 لتركيب البروتين.

concepts.explanation: The material connects AlphaFold2 with protein structure prediction and the 2024 Chemistry Nobel discussion. Computational protein design is a related but distinct contribution.
concepts.question: Which scientific task is associated with AlphaFold2?

concepts.explanation: FermiNet models quantum wavefunctions and electronic systems. LapNet addresses efficient neural-network variational Monte Carlo computation.
concepts.question: Which pair belongs to the course quantum-mechanics examples?

concepts.explanation: GNoME uses graph neural-network methods in materials discovery, including crystal structure and stability prediction.
concepts.question: Which application is associated with GNoME?

concepts.explanation: MatterGen uses diffusion-based generation to design inorganic materials under property constraints. It can be adapted toward required characteristics.
concepts.question: Which model generates inorganic materials with desired properties?
distractors: GPT-1 as the cited materials model
k-NN as the cited generative model

concepts.explanation: DeePMD-kit combines deep-learning potentials with first-principles ideas and high-performance computing for molecular dynamics.
concepts.question: Which scientific application best matches DeePMD-kit?
